newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank satisfied with zloty at 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank satisfied with zloty at 2.5 pct.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is satisfied with the zloty's exchange rate at 2.5 percent from the trading band centre, the head of the central bank's foreign exchange department Krzysztof Majczuk told Reuters.
"The central bank is satisfied with the level of the zloty at 2.5 percent from the parity rate," Majczuk said.
The NBP has been buying dollars and marks on the market since last Thursday to weaken the zloty, stubbornly rising on the back of foreign entry into zloty instruments.

The central bank long kept the zloty at around 3.1 percent above the parity rate but began pushing the local currency down last week and set off a flood of foreign investor purchases of Polish treasuries.
NBP deputy president Witold Kozinski earlier said that through the weaker zloty the bank wanted to help exporters and curb Poland's widening trade deficit.
